title: Chapters 8.1 & 8.2 — Graphing f(x) = ax² and f(x) = ax² + c (30 Cards)

cards.front: What is a [[kw:quadratic function]]?
cards.back: A nonlinear function that can be written in standard form $$y = ax^2 + bx + c$$ where $a \ne 0$. The graph is a parabola.

cards.front: What is a [[kw:parabola]]?
cards.back: The U-shaped graph of a quadratic function. It opens upward if $a > 0$, downward if $a < 0$.

cards.front: What is the [[kw:vertex]] of a parabola?
cards.back: The lowest point (if it opens up) or highest point (if it opens down). For $f(x)=ax^2$, the vertex is $(0,0)$.

cards.front: What is the [[kw:axis of symmetry]]?
cards.back: The vertical line through the vertex that divides the parabola into two mirror-image halves. For $f(x)=ax^2$, it is $x=0$.

cards.front: What is the domain and range of $f(x)=x^2$?
cards.back: Domain: all real numbers. Range: $y \ge 0$ (since $x^2$ is never negative).
When $a > 0$. The vertex is a minimum. Example: $f(x)=2x^2$.
cards.front: When does the graph of $f(x)=ax^2$ open upward?
When does the graph of $f(x)=ax^2$ open downward?
cards.back: When $a < 0$. The vertex is a maximum. Example: $f(x)=-3x^2$.

cards.front: What happens to the graph when $a > 1$ in $f(x)=ax^2$?
cards.back: [[imp:Vertical stretch]] — the parabola becomes narrower than $f(x)=x^2$. The y-values are multiplied by $a$.

cards.front: What happens to the graph when $0 < a < 1$ in $f(x)=ax^2$?
cards.back: [[imp:Vertical shrink]] — the parabola becomes wider than $f(x)=x^2$. The y-values are smaller in magnitude.

cards.front: What two transformations occur when $a < 0$ in $f(x)=ax^2$?
cards.back: 1) [[imp:Reflection]] in the x-axis (opens downward). 2) Vertical stretch (if $|a|>1$) or vertical shrink (if $0<|a|<1$).
Opens downward (reflection), wider (vertical shrink by factor $\frac{1}{3}$). Vertex still at $(0,0)$, axis $x=0$.
cards.front: Describe the graph of $g(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2$ compared to $f(x)=x^2$.
How does the value of $|a|$ affect the width of $y=ax^2$?
cards.back: If $|a| > 1$, the graph is narrower (stretch). If $0 < |a| < 1$, the graph is wider (shrink). The larger $|a|$, the narrower the parabola.
Width: $2 - (-2) = 4$ meters. Depth: at $x=2$, $y = \frac{1}{4}(4) = 1$ meter. Depth = $1 - 0 = 1$ meter.
cards.front: A satellite dish has cross section $y = \frac{1}{4}x^2$ with domain $-2 \le x \le 2$. Find its width and depth.
How do you find the width of a parabolic dish from its quadratic model?
cards.back: Width is the horizontal distance between the leftmost and rightmost $x$-values (length of the given domain).
Depth is the vertical distance from the vertex (minimum) to the rim (maximum $y$ on the domain). Depth = $y_{\text{max}} - y_{\text{min}}$.
cards.front: How do you find the depth of a parabolic dish from $y=ax^2$?
How does the graph of $f(x) = ax^2 + c$ compare to $f(x) = ax^2$?
cards.back: It is a [[imp:vertical translation]] by $c$ units. If $c > 0$, shift up; if $c < 0$, shift down. The vertex moves from $(0,0)$ to $(0,c)$.
$$ (0, c) $$ The axis of symmetry is always $x = 0$.
cards.front: What is the vertex of $f(x) = ax^2 + c$?
Graph $g(x) = x^2 - 2$ and compare to $f(x) = x^2$.
cards.back: Both open up, same axis $x=0$. Vertex of $g$ is $(0,-2)$, a vertical translation 2 units down from $f$'s vertex $(0,0)$.
[[imp:Vertical stretch]] by factor 4 (narrower) and [[imp:vertical translation]] 1 unit up. Vertex $(0,1)$.
cards.front: Graph $g(x) = 4x^2 + 1$ and describe the transformations from $f(x) = x^2$.
What two transformations does $h(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 + 4$ apply to $f(x) = x^2$?
cards.back: 1. Reflection in the x‑axis and vertical shrink by $\frac{1}{4}$ (wider, opens down). 2. Vertical translation 4 units up. Vertex $(0,4)$.
$$ g(x) = (3x^2 - 1) + 3 = 3x^2 + 2 $$ The graph of $g$ is shifted up 3 units from $f$.
cards.front: How do you write $g(x)$ in standard form if $f(x) = 3x^2 - 1$ and $g(x) = f(x) + 3$?
What is the domain and range of $f(x) = ax^2 + c$?
cards.back: Domain: all real numbers. Range: if $a > 0$, $y \ge c$; if $a < 0$, $y \le c$.

cards.front: What is a [[kw:zero]] of a function?
cards.back: An $x$-value where $f(x) = 0$. It is also the $x$-intercept of the graph.

cards.front: How do you find the zeros of $f(x) = ax^2 + c$?
cards.back: Set $ax^2 + c = 0$ and solve for $x$: $$ x = \pm \sqrt{-\frac{c}{a}} $$ Real zeros exist only if $ -c/a \ge 0 $.

cards.front: Find the zeros of $f(x) = x^2 - 36$.
cards.back: $$ x^2 - 36 = 0 \to x^2 = 36 \to x = \pm 6 $$ Zeros are $-6$ and $6$.
Set $-16t^2 + 64 = 0 \to t^2 = 4 \to t = 2$ seconds (take positive root only).
cards.front: An egg is dropped from 64 feet: $f(t) = -16t^2 + 64$. When does it hit the ground?

cards.back: Time cannot be negative in this context; $t = 0$ is the moment of the drop. Only $t \ge 0$ is physically meaningful.
cards.front: Why are only nonnegative values of $t$ used in the egg drop problem?
Does $f(x) = 2x^2 + 8$ have real zeros? Why or why not?
cards.back: No. $a$ and $c$ are both positive, so $ -c/a $ is negative. $x^2 = -4$ has no real solutions. The vertex $(0,8)$ is above the x‑axis and the parabola opens up.

cards.front: How does increasing $c$ affect the zeros of $f(x) = ax^2 + c$?
cards.back: The graph shifts up, so the zeros move closer together. If $c$ becomes large enough, the vertex rises above the x‑axis and there are no real zeros.
